gloss: sweets; desserts (a stylish, modern-feeling word for confections, especially Western-style)

definitions.gloss: sweets; desserts; pastries (Western-style or modern Japanese-style confections)
definitions.explanation: Sweet foods, especially Western-style desserts such as cakes, tarts, parfaits, and pastries, but also stylishly presented Japanese sweets. The word entered everyday Japanese in the 2000s and now strongly implies fashionable, café-style confections suitable for posting to social media. It is more upscale and trendy in feel than お{菓子|かし}, which can mean any kind of snack or sweet.

examples.japanese: スイーツ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大好|だいす}き→大好き：02911_daisuki⟧だ。
⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧スイーツ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{店|みせ}→お店：21164_omise⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: A new sweets shop has opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦{季節|きせつ}{限定|げんてい}→季節限定：09823_kisetsugentei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧スイーツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|で}かけた→出かける：00833_dekakeru⟧。

examples.english: Convenience-store sweets have been improving in quality year by year, and many rival those of famous shops.

notes:
スイーツ is the English plural "sweets" naturalized into Japanese as a fashionable, lifestyle-oriented word for desserts. It became popular in the 2000s, partly through TV food coverage, and now refers to a broad category of café and shop confections — especially photogenic Western-style desserts like cakes, tarts, parfaits, macarons, and pancakes.

USAGE:
- Café and dessert-shop menus
- Convenience-store premium dessert lines (⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧スイーツ)
- Hotel afternoon-tea sets and seasonal fairs
- Social-media food posts
- スイーツ has a distinctly cosmopolitan, Instagrammable connotation. A handful of ⟦{煎餅|せんべい}→煎餅：04958_senbei⟧ would not normally be called スイーツ.
- The word can be used as a count noun in phrases like スイーツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{二|ふた}つ→二つ：02953_futatsu⟧⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧ "to pick two desserts."
- For polite restaurant menus, ⟦デザート→デザート：00036_dezaato⟧ is more common than スイーツ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- スイーツ⟦{店|てん}→店：10011_ten⟧ / スイーツ⟦ショップ→ショップ：08913_shoppu⟧: dessert shop
- ⟦{季節|きせつ}{限定|げんてい}→季節限定：09823_kisetsugentei⟧スイーツ: seasonal limited-edition dessert
- ⟦コンビニ→コンビニ：01081_konbini⟧スイーツ: convenience-store dessert
- {和|わ}スイーツ: "Japanese-style sweets" — a marketing term for Japanese confections styled as modern desserts
- スイーツ⟦{男子|だんし}→男子：03425_danshi⟧: a man who enjoys eating and shopping for sweets
- スイーツ{巡|めぐ}り: a sweets tour, going from shop to shop

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧: sweets, snacks — the general native word, covering everything from rice crackers and chocolate bars to traditional Japanese confections. Much broader than スイーツ.
- ⟦デザート→デザート：00036_dezaato⟧: dessert — usually a course at the end of a meal
- ⟦{洋菓子|ようがし}→洋菓子：04998_yougashi⟧: Western-style confections (cakes, cookies, etc.) — a more traditional category label, somewhat overlapping with スイーツ but less trendy in feel
- ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧: traditional Japanese confections (e.g., ⟦{大福|だいふく}→大福：12173_daifuku⟧, ⟦{羊羹|ようかん}→羊羹：05002_youkan⟧); not normally called スイーツ except in modern marketing as "{和|わ}スイーツ"
- ⟦{甘|あま}い→甘い：00617_amai⟧もの: sweet things — a casual, native expression for "sweet stuff" in general
